newsitem.title: USA: Former U.S. astronaut's son found drowned in car.
newsitem.headline: Former U.S. astronaut's son found drowned in car.

text.p: Police said on Thursday that one of two dead men found in a car submerged in a local lake was the son of former U.S. astronaut Brewster Shaw.
They said the body of Brandon Shaw, a 20-year-old student at the University of Texas at Austin, was discovered on Wednesday after a teenaged suspect in a string of carjackings led police to the site.
Shaw and Juan Cotera, 25, were found dead in the trunk of Shaw's 1982 Volvo. The car had been driven into Town Lake, which is in the centre of Austin.
Police said they believe the two victims were captured in separate incidents, but died at the same time.

Cotera and a female friend were robbed at gunpoint on Monday night. The woman, who was also sexually assaulted, escaped and went to police, but Cotera was taken away by the robbers in the woman's car.
Shaw had not been reported missing before his body was discovered. "We are trying to determine at what point Shaw became a victim," Austin Police Department Mike Burgess said.

A NASA spokesman at Johnson Space Centre in Houston said Brewster Shaw became an astronaut in 1978 and flew on three space shuttle missions and was director of shuttle operations before leaving NASA in 1994.
Shaw and his wife were said to now be living in Huntington Beach, Calif.

Burgess said two 17-year-old boys had been charged in the string of carjackings, but had not yet been formally accused of murder in the death of the two men. Both were being held in Travis County Jail.
